autonomous_processes: None during the active task: after preparation and between stroke actions, the generated course, ball, hand, and legal transitions do not change without a new input.
A legal stroke updates the ball, spent-card list, and transcript synchronously in the input handler; CSS hover, selection, and drag transitions are presentation-only.
Certification can fetch a result and render a fresh course after rejection, but that is post-submission administrative handling rather than an autonomous outcome phase.

clause_i.reason: For the simplified stroke mode, an observation-free policy q cannot choose the optimal first card and direction across seeds: the generator reflects the course, transforms directions, and shuffles the cards, while I_t is identical before the first action.

clause_ii.reason: The current screenshot exposes the static isometric course, ball, surfaces, ramps, cup, and unused pictured hand. A bounded window of 0 ms (one frame) is sufficient to compute the next legal card and direction; waiting does not change that choice.

clause_iii.reason: There is no non-clock autonomous task-state evolution H_t to H_t^tau between actions. Waiting does not make a legal stroke unavailable or less effective; only a synchronous stroke changes position and spent cards. Any deadline passage is clock loss alone and cannot supply the required strict non-clock Q loss.

common_visible_process: No common visible autonomous process exists. The visible course is a fixed generated board; there is no motion, decay, timer-driven rule, physics tick, or expiring stroke opportunity.

pre_run.reason: No autonomous outcome phase exists. The seven generated route strokes can be completed from the static visible course before the administrative certification, so the pre-run phase test is not applicable and cannot change the mathematical No.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 4 is the seven-stroke, 11x9, sand/water/ramp course profile; simplified interaction is card selection followed by a compass-button click; observation_window_ms is 0 and frames_per_observation is 1.
Generation is seeded and static: it constructs the transformed course, cards, and route solution, shuffles cards, and returns public state and ground truth without a task clock or autonomous phase.

The visible simplified UI binds card clicks and compass clicks to dispatch; dispatch synchronously validates a stroke, updates ball/used/events, redraws, and updates status. Render installs the controls and performs no scheduled progression.

The only asynchronous fetch is certification after the transcript is assembled; success terminates or rejection renders a fresh course, so it is administrative submission rather than an active between-action mechanic.
The card and button transitions are hover/selection/drag presentation styles and do not alter course state or stroke legality.

The grader replays an ordered transcript against the fixed public course and cards, checks static before/after states and input source, then accepts only the cup position with every card used; it has no timestamps or autonomous evolution.
The normal UI solver performs each pictured stroke before clicking certification; its 120 ms waits are harness waits between synchronous updates, not task-state progression.
Verification only loads the exported result and delegates to the Cloudstep Caddie replay grader.
